CITM315 · Academic project

Linux Administration and a Complete Group Apache Web Project

Adnan Khan

I completed four Linux administration assignments and worked on a shared Fedora web-server project. This walkthrough covers the individual command-line exercises and the whole team build: VM access, Apache, firewall configuration, the website, media delivery and client-side downloads.

Tools and environment

PuTTY and student VPN; Linux shell, Bash, sed, awk, systemctl, RPM, tar, cpio; VMware Workstation; Fedora 44 Server; Tailscale; Apache HTTP Server; HTML.

Individual labs and group project. May-July 2026.

Connect and inspect the Linux environment

I connected through the student VPN and PuTTY, checked my identity with whoami and id, and used pwd, ls -la, man and uname to understand the session. I also searched configuration and log directories. Permission-denied responses marked the limits of the regular account.

Work with files, links and storage

I created and inspected files, compared a hard link with a symbolic link, and moved the original file. The hard link retained its inode relationship while the symbolic link retained the old path. I then used df, du and /etc/fstab to distinguish filesystem capacity, directory usage and mount configuration.

Inspect memory, hardware, services and logs

I checked memory with free, swap with swapon --show and CPU information with lscpu. systemctl status sshd showed the service state; process listings connected the shell to its session. A top snapshot and the rsyslog authpriv destination added operational context.

Process text and practise shell control flow

I redirected normal output and errors, transformed text with sed, and filtered colon-separated records with awk. The Blue-record calculation returned Honda 35000, Ford 75000 and Nissan 30000. I also compared exported variables in child shells and wrote a three-prompt word-mapping script.

Inspect archives and installed software

I compared compress and gzip output, created tar and cpio archives, and listed their members. I then used RPM to inspect openssh-server metadata, supplied files and requirements, with ldd for runtime libraries. The archive evidence records creation and listing; a restore would be a separate validation step.

Prepare the group VM and remote access

Next, the project used a Fedora 44 Server VM in VMware Workstation with the base environment, bridged network access and Tailscale connectivity. The recorded addresses were 192.168.1.121 locally and 100.100.214.52 through Tailscale. SSH provided the administration path.

Install Apache and check the service

Next, httpd was installed using dnf, its package version was checked, and the service was enabled with systemctl enable --now httpd. The screenshots record httpd-2.4.68-1.fc44.x86_64 and an active Apache service. This established the web service before adding our custom content.

Allow HTTP and configure the server name

Next, the HTTP firewall service was added permanently and the firewall was reloaded. ServerName www.group9.ca:80 was set in httpd.conf and Apache was restarted. The directive identifies the Apache server name; the browser tests establish access within the tested client environment.

Validate the initial page and build the homepage

Next, the default Fedora page was retrieved before the custom site was added. The homepage was built with text, image and audio content, then linked to the About and Downloads pages. A curl response and the completed browser page connect the server setup to the published lab content.

Create the About and Downloads pages

I created about.html, download.html and sample.txt under /var/www/html. The Downloads page links to the text file using the download attribute, and both subpages link back to the homepage. I checked the rendered pages as part of the shared site.

Test the full range of site content

Next, direct retrieval of text, PDF, image, audio and video content was checked. These checks covered more than the homepage: each request asked Apache for a different file type under the document root. The captured browser responses show the media reached the client.

Confirm the download and explain the request path

Next, the text-file download was confirmed on a Windows client; the directory listing records sample.txt at 48 bytes. The complete path is browser request, Apache on the Fedora VM, content under /var/www/html, and a response or saved file on the client. SSH administration uses a separate service path.

What I learned

  • Diagnose the relevant filesystem, service and package instead of relying on one command.
  • Validate a website from both the server configuration and client response.
  • Treat the team deployment as one complete system and document the workflow clearly.

Source: the full CITM315 portfolio supplied for this project. Evidence is from the original coursework; this edition adds no new lab test results. Repeated captures and earlier drafts are consolidated. Revised design summaries are labelled, and sensitive identifiers are masked.
